findings.text: Host fault injector for data aborts from exclusive atomic access. When the virtual CPU runs in a nested context with second stage enabled it delegates to the nested injector. Otherwise it raises a synchronous external abort for the supplied address and then adjusts the trapped syndrome to report the exclusive atomic fault class, signalling that the guest exception is now pending.

Size fault injector for a guest address beyond the supported physical range. It rebuilds the fault address from the trapped intermediate address plus the high fault offset, raises a synchronous external abort whose instruction versus data character follows the original trap, and then for most guests clears the low syndrome field to denote a level zero address size fault. Guests in 32 bit mode without extended translation keep the plain external abort because they cannot represent the size fault.

Small helper that stores a register width value into a byte buffer using the requested access width. Supported widths are single byte, half word, word and double word, each handled through a width matched temporary before copying the requested number of bytes to the destination.

Main data abort path for guest physical accesses that miss second stage mapping. It decodes validity, direction, width and target register from the trapped syndrome, attempts in kernel bus handling, and otherwise prepares user exit structures. A kernel handled access advances the virtual CPU past the instruction and reports handled, while a userspace handled access reports that an exit is pending with address, width, direction and data staged.

When the trapped syndrome carries no valid decode information the abort path does not attempt emulation. Protected guests receive an injected data abort exception, guests whose virtual machine opted into no syndrome userspace handling receive a dedicated exit carrying sanitised syndrome and fault address, and all other cases fail without emulation.

Certain translation and permission fault classes that carry a load store type field are never emulated in kernel. When that field is non zero the abort path forwards the whole access to userspace through a dedicated sixty four byte access exit that carries the fault address and the syndrome with fault status removed.

Host hypervisor address space globals comprise a page table root pointer guarded by a dedicated mutex, an identity map address interval with its vector, a variable width address size value, and a base address for device mappings. The interval, vector, address size and device base become read only after early initialisation.
Range walker helper that applies a callback over a second stage interval while permitting voluntary scheduling. It is the scheduling tolerant form of the underlying range applicator.

Eager huge page splitting estimates its table demand from the length of the interval, counting upper level tables only when the minimum block level allows them plus mid level tables for the whole span. A helper decides to pause when scheduling is needed, when the address space lock is contended, or when the split cache holds fewer free objects than the estimate for one chunk.

Chunked splitter walks the requested interval in bounded chunks. If the cache or scheduler asks to pause it releases the address space write lock, yields, tops up the split cache on a best effort basis, and reacquires the lock before continuing. It validates that the stage two root still exists on each iteration and stops on first split or allocation failure, with a zero chunk size meaning no work.
A memory slot counts as dirty logging when it has a dirty bitmap allocated and is not marked read only.

Remote translation cache maintenance offers whole virtual machine and address range forms. Protected mode routes both through the non host hypervisor call with the protected handle, while non protected mode uses direct hypervisor calls for the whole machine case and a ranged invalidation primitive for the range case. Both forms always report success.

Second stage memory operations wrap host allocation with page accounting. Cache backed zeroed page allocation accounts on success, exact size allocation pairs host zeroed allocation with positive accounting, and exact size release pairs negative accounting with host release. Hypervisor memcache allocation and release similarly pair host page primitives with conditional stage two accounting.

Unlinked stage two tables are reclaimed after a grace period, with the table level carried in page private data across the callback. Reference handling pins and releases host pages, with the stage two release variant withdrawing accounting when the final reference drops. Address translation uses host direct map helpers and guest cache maintenance delegates to dedicated clean and invalidate primitives.

Cache flush coverage spans a single interval, a single memory slot derived from its base guest frame and page count, a whole virtual machine by iterating all slots, and nested second stage address spaces by iterating valid nested roots over their full physical size. Slot and machine forms operate on the primary second stage root.

Whole machine flushing holds the read side source lock across the operation and the address space lock for writing while iterating slots and nested roots. Nested flushing requires the address space write lock to be already held and performs no locking itself.
Protected mode sharing tracker records a page frame number with a reference count and tree linkage. The tree root and its guarding mutex are statically initialised and empty at boot.

Host userspace mapping probe walks the host page tables for a single address with interrupts disabled to guard against concurrent teardown. It rejects unexpected table levels, asks the caller to replay the fault when no valid leaf is present or when teardown raced, and otherwise reports the host block size implied by the leaf level.

Second stage table operations table binds cache backed and exact allocation, exact release, deferred unlinked table release, page reference and count helpers, host address translation, and guest data and instruction cache maintenance. The userspace walker table binds only address translation because leaf lookup needs no other callback.

Protected mode hypervisor memcache top up is a no op when protected mode is disabled. Otherwise it lazily allocates the backing mapping structure on first use and then ensures at least the requested number of pages using host allocation and address translation.

Write protection coverage spans a single interval, a single memory slot, and all nested second stage roots. Slot protection resolves the slot from its identifier, protects the corresponding guest physical span on the primary root, protects every valid nested root over its full size, and then invalidates translation caches for the affected slot. Nested protection additionally refreshes virtual control state mappings.

Splitting and write protection serialise on the address space write lock. Per slot splitting requires the slots lock on entry and acquires the address space lock internally, per slot protection acquires the address space lock internally and flushes translation caches after release, and chunked splitting, dirty log enablement and nested protection all require the address space write lock to be already held.

Masked dirty log enablement converts a bit mask within a slot offset into a guest physical interval from its first to last set bits and write protects that interval on the primary root. When manual protection with initial set semantics is active it also eagerly splits huge pages in the same interval, and it always write protects nested roots as well.

Block mapping at second stage is allowed for single pages unconditionally, while larger mappings must satisfy three constraints. Protected mode accepts only mid level block size, the guest and userspace bases must share the same offset modulo the block size so that block placement does not misalign pages, and the aligned block containing the faulting address must lie fully inside the memory slot.

Transparent huge page adjustment attempts mid level block mapping only when alignment and containment permit and when the host mapping itself is at least that large. On success it aligns both guest frame and host page numbers down to the block boundary and reports block size, otherwise it reports single page size. A companion helper reports huge page shift for hugetlb areas and base page shift elsewhere.

Tag sanitisation is skipped without memory tagging support and for the shared zero page. Hugetlb folios are tagged once with per page tag clearing guarded by a one time attempt, while normal pages are attempted and marked individually. Companion predicates test the allowed tag flag and exclude non cacheable and device memory types, and memcache selection plus top up choose the conventional per virtual CPU cache or the protected cache with matching top up path based on protected mode and the hardware address space minimum.
The width helper only defines behaviour for four discrete widths. Callers must guarantee one of those widths because any other length would leave the source pointer unset before the copy.

The chunked splitter temporarily releases its write lock to reschedule and replenish its cache, so it revalidates the table root after each pause. Allocation failure during top up is treated as best effort termination rather than a fatal error, and callers must tolerate a partially split range.

Probing host page table level races with userspace teardown. The probe disables interrupts across the walk and treats missing or invalid leaves as a request to replay the fault instead of proceeding with a stale size.

A guest device access completes in one of five externally visible states: completed in kernel with data staged for a read, exited for userspace device emulation, exited for no syndrome handling when enabled, exited for sixty four byte load store handling, or converted into a guest abort for protected guests and invalid syndromes. Kernel completion and userspace exits are distinguished by return value and by statistics counters.
Hardware poison reporting delivers an access error machine check signal to the current thread for the supplied userspace address and severity hint.
Guest exit interface provides separate reasons for standard device emulation, for no syndrome handling, and for large load store handling, plus a dedicated bus identifier for device bus operations.
